exposure: first hemoglobin A1C recorded in pregnancy
cohort: 3570 pregnancies complicated by gestational diabetes mellitus delivering singleton live-born infants at ≥34 weeks of gestation
finding: A clinically pragmatic model using information routinely available in the third trimester of pregnancy, including large for gestational age, polyhydramnios, older maternal age, early pregnancy body mass index, first hemoglobin A1C recorded in pregnancy, nulliparity, insulin treatment, and preeclampsia, can predict intrapartum primary CD risk with reasonable reliability in pregnancies complicated by gestational diabetes mellitus.
mod_finding: Nulliparity was found to be significantly associated with cesarean delivery in pregnancies complicated by gestational diabetes mellitus.
